description: THIS FILE ONLY WORKS IF THE RENOVATE GITHUB APP IS INSTALLED ON THE ORG. It is not a
workflow and nothing in CI runs it. As of 2026-08-13 the App had never run here — no
pull request, no dependency dashboard issue, no branch — which is why the GitHub Actions
below sat two majors behind until they were bumped by hand, and why the Node 20
deprecation warning appeared on every run.
If you are reading this because dependencies look stale, check the App before the config.
`description`, NOT `//`. Renovate validates every key and rejects unknown ones, so a `//`
comment key does not document the file, it stops the bot: Renovate refused this config
on 2026-08-14 and opened no dependency pull request for the twelve days after. The lesson
is the one `tooling/lighthouse/lighthouserc.json` already carries in its own header — JSON
has no comments, and inventing one breaks whichever tool parses the file.
`commitMessageTopic` drops Renovate's default word `dependency` from every subject. The
title lint applies CLAUDE.md's 72-character rule to what lands after squash, which is the
subject plus ` (#N)`, so the real budget is 65. Renovate's default produced
`chore(deps): update dependency @changesets/changelog-github to v1.0.1` at 69 characters on
2026-09-14 and a patch bump that should have automerged sat red instead. The word carries
no information the scope `(deps)` does not already carry. `bump` for the action is two
characters shorter than `update`, which is what puts the longest name in the tree,
`@fontsource-variable/hanken-grotesk`, inside the budget at a normal version. Measured,
not guessed: the five longest subjects the tree can produce were computed before this
landed, and that one was the only one over.
`group:allNonMajor` puts every minor and patch into ONE pull request per run instead of one
each. On 2026-09-21 ticking thirteen queued updates opened thirteen PRs, each with its own CI
run, each falling behind main as the previous one merged, which meant thirteen update-branch
rounds and a notification for every step. Majors stay separate because each needs a CLAUDE.md
toolchain row and a reason, not a merge. `prConcurrentLimit` and `prHourlyLimit` bound the
rest: two open at a time is one to review and one warming up.
Two of the pins live in CLAUDE.md's toolchain table as well as in their files, and repo:check
assertion 7 holds them equal. The first grouped PR on 2026-09-21 bumped `.nvmrc` and the
Dockerfile to a new Node minor, left the table row at the old one, and sat red. The two regex
`customManagers` below teach Renovate the Node and pnpm rows, so a runtime bump carries its
table row in the same commit. `docs/self-hosting.md` and the hosting page no longer name the
version at all: they point at `.nvmrc` and `packageManager`, which cannot drift.
The same PR bumped tsdown `^0.22` to `^0.23.0`. A caret on 0.x does not cover the next minor,
so Renovate rewrites the catalog range, assertion 6 sees a pin the table does not, and the
whole group is blocked. A 0.x minor is a major in every way that matters here: it needs a
table row and a reason. The rule below takes them out of the group and out of automerge.

packageRules.description: Patch AND minor updates automerge once CI is green. CI is the review: 1,000-odd unit tests, contract replays over recorded provider bytes, e2e over a socket, and repo:check holding the catalog to the CLAUDE.md toolchain table, so a bump that changes a pinned range fails assertion 6 and never automerges. Majors stay manual; each needs a toolchain row and a reason. GitHub Actions are exempted by the NEXT rule rather than by an exclusion here: `excludeManagers` is not a Renovate option and never was, and it is the second half of why this config was rejected. Later packageRules override earlier ones, so the github-actions rule below turns automerge back off for that manager.

GitHub Actions are never automerged, and are pinned to a commit SHA. release.yml runs with contents:write, packages:write and id-token:write and mints npm provenance, so a compromised third-party action executes inside the job that signs our releases. The repo already checksums the one gitleaks tarball it downloads, with the comment that piping an unverified download into a shell is a poor look in the job whose purpose is supply-chain hygiene — the same standard now applies to the code around the publish. repo:check assertion 47 holds it.
typescript 7.x is the Go rewrite, not a 5.x successor. See the Why column in CLAUDE.md.
@types/node must stay major-matched to the Node pin or it types the wrong runtime.
pnpm stays on 10. pnpm 11.0.x reimplemented publish natively and broke the OIDC exchange; see the Why column in CLAUDE.md and operating.md B8 before lifting this.

A minor bump of a 0.x package (tsdown, drizzle-orm, drizzle-kit) rewrites the caret range in the catalog, which is a pin change the toolchain table has to carry with a reason. Treated like a major: its own PR, never automerged, out of the all-non-major group so it cannot hold the rest red. `groupName: null` clears the name the preset set; a later packageRule wins.

customManagers.description: The Node row of CLAUDE.md's toolchain table. Same depName and datasource as the .nvmrc manager, so the two land in one branch.
The pnpm row of the same table. The npm manager updates `packageManager` in package.json, hash included; this keeps the table on the same version.
